title: courier.notification.suppressed payload
description: The `data` payload of the `courier.notification.suppressed` event: a send was skipped. There is no `message_id` here, and that is the point — nothing was rendered, nothing was addressed and nothing left, so there is no notification to be about. The entity is the recipient, which is why the catalog's subject for this type is the recipient rather than the notification. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

user_id.description: The user the send was for. A uuid from identity, not a cafaye-prefixed id: see D7. This is the identity the envelope's `subject` carries too, pending D8 on whether the recipient means the user or the address.

notification_type.description: Which of courier's three messages was skipped. Preferences are per type and per channel, so "off" is only ever about one of these.

email.description: The address that was not written to. Two of the three reasons are about the address rather than the type, which is why it is here and not only in the suppression list.

reason.description: Why the send was skipped. `preference_off` is the user turning the type off in their own settings; `address_suppressed` is a previous `courier.email.bounced` or `.complained`; `rate_limited` is courier declining to send more than the provider will take. The three come from the catalog row for this type — only `preference_off` is reachable in courier today, and the others arrive with the code that produces them. See D8 for the spelling of these values.
